title: POC Weekly: Reliability & Incident Follow-up
topics: Observability: traces, logs, and request ids
Next steps for stability and benchmarking
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last week's incidents: increased 5xx rate and intermittent timeouts during peak ingestion. SE reviewed server-side metrics and suggested client retry/backoff tuning plus tokenization and batching tweaks. Action items assigned for logs correlation, RBAC check for dedicated pool, and follow-up load test. Redwood to share incident timeline and updated runbook.
transcript:
Header: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: Fireflies
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Caleb (Redwood CSM), Maria (Lexicon ML), Ethan (Lexicon Platform), Sophie (Lexicon PM)
---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: run through the incidents from monday, what we saw in telemetry, tuning we did yesterday, and next steps. should be about 45 minutes.
[00:18] Maria: yep thanks, we got the notes — we had a spike of what looked like 5xx errors and a bunch of client-side timeouts when our ingestion pipeline hit a burst, around 11:20–11:40 utc.
[00:31] Priya: to clarify, were those 5xxs originating from the Redwood API gateway or from the dedicated pool instances?
[00:40] Ethan: we traced to the gateway first; proxy returned 502/503s. but when we cross-referenced request ids, a subset also had kube-level restarts on our side, so there's some interaction.
[00:55] Priya: got it. we pulled the host-level metrics and saw cpu scheduling spikes on a few workers plus increased queue latency. KV cache hit rates dropped because of cache eviction on one of the pods — possibly due to an uneven routing event.
[01:12] Maria: the interesting bit: our client logs show backoffs but the retry window is fairly short, so some requests end up timing out at the client at ~1s.
[01:25] Jordan: yeah, and the POC default retry policy is aggressive by default to keep latency low; in production you'd normally lengthen backoff or enable exponential jitter.
[01:35] Sophie: can you explain the impact matrix — i.e., what percentage of requests saw 5xx vs timeouts vs token-level failures?
[01:47] Priya: rough numbers from yesterday's window: ~2.3% returned 5xx, 4.1% hit client-side timeouts (>= 1s), and tokenization errors were negligible (<0.1%). the real user-facing pain was the timeouts during peak concurrency.
[02:08] Ethan: and we were also hitting a rate limit on our end because we have a pipeline fan-out. some of the client library calls were not pooling connections properly so we were opening too many concurrent streams and then hitting the gateway throttle at ~1200 rps.
[02:25] Jordan: that throttle is important — we can either increase burst quotas for the POC or implement a client-side concurrency cap. what's your preference for the next week?
[02:35] Maria: we'd like to try client-side caps first; it's quicker on our side. but we also want the burst quota bump to run the load test later.
[02:45] Priya: actionable: we'll provide recommended caps and a tuned retry/backoff config. also, we propose enabling prefix/KV cache pinning for common prompts so caching stays warm across bursty traffic.
[03:02] Maria: how do we pin? we don't want to rework the prompt infra too much.
[03:08] Priya: simple change: add a deterministic prefix to common prompts and opt into the cache policy in the request metadata. i'll share a snippet in the notes.
[03:20] Jordan: quick incident timeline: our SRE traced an increase in HTTP 503s at 11:19 UTC, with a follow-on burst of client retries from 11:20 to 11:40, which produced amplified load and caused an extra 12% CPU on two nodes, leading to eviction churn.
[03:38] Ethan: we saw a pod restart around 11:27, probably due to oom or liveness probe. logs show spike in memory from large batched requests.
[03:48] Priya: that aligns — large batched sequences with long context will push memory. we recommended yesterday to lower max batch size for that route from 32 to 12 for now. did you apply that?
[03:58] Maria: yes we pushed batch_size=12 on monday after your suggestion. graphs improved but the gateway errors persisted for another 20 mins.
[04:08] Priya: sounds like the root cause is multi-factor — routing imbalance causing cold cache + bursty large batches + short client retries. solution set is both client and server: concurrency caps, adjusted batch sizes, cache pinning, and better routing fallbacks.
[04:22] Sophie: what about the retry semantics — should we be adding idempotency tokens for dedup?
[04:29] Priya: great question. for generation calls, idempotency helps if you want de-dup, but typically we rely on request ids and the platform's dedup window is short. if you have downstream idempotency needs, add a client-level request id header.
[04:41] Jordan: also note: we can enable a per-route soft quota that will return 429 earlier rather than letting requests pile up and cause 5xx. customers often prefer deterministic 429s to unpredictable 5xxs.
[04:54] Ethan: i'd prefer that. 429s reduce uncertainty.
[05:00] Priya: ok we'll propose a soft-quota policy for your POC route.
[05:05] [05:05] Caleb: quick point on observability — we stitched together the logs you shared and our APM traces but we still need a single correlation id across client -> gateway -> worker. can we set a header in your client?
[05:18] Maria: yes we can emit X-Request-Id on all calls.
[05:21] Priya: perfect. that'll make the post-mortem much cleaner. please include those traces in the slack thread.
[05:28] Sophie: can you also share the incident runbook updates? last time we weren't sure which pager to escalate to.
[05:34] Jordan: we'll send the updated runbook; note we added on-call rotations and a triage checklist.
[05:40] Priya: other tuning: quantization profile changes we tested yesterday lowered memory by ~18% on the model runner for the same latency. might help reduce the OOM risk.
[05:52] Ethan: is that safe for quality? we run clinical summarization, so hallucinations are sensitive.
[05:58] Priya: yes we tested the ngram-preserve setting; small quality delta but within your eval thresholds. we'll share the eval report.
[06:07] Maria: any quick wins we can apply today?
[06:10] Priya: yes: enable client concurrency cap, increase client timeout to 3 seconds with exponential jitter, set batch_size=12 for ingestion route, and add X-Request-Id header.
[06:22] Jordan: we'll also provision a temporary burst quota bump of +30% for your POC for the scheduled load test, and open a ticket to monitor gateway queue depth.
[06:32] Sophie: timeline on the ticket?
[06:34] Jordan: i'll create it today and assign to Priya; target is 48 hours for initial telemetry reports and 7 days for a follow-up after load testing.
[06:45] Maria: ok that sounds good.
[06:49] [10:00] — later section —
[10:00] Priya: a couple notes from the debug dump: some hostnames in the logs had slightly different model tags — one pod was running v1.2.0-rc instead of v1.2.1 stable; we traced a mismatch in the rollout that led to slightly different kernel selection which increased memory.
[10:21] Ethan: ah that could explain the eviction on that node. can you include the node/pod ids in the post mortem?
[10:27] Priya: yes will include.
[10:29] Jordan: for the next test, please coordinate with us for a 2-hour window in the afternoon so we can watch metrics in real time.
[10:36] Sophie: we'll block thursday 14:00–16:00 UTC.
[10:40] Jordan: perfect.
[10:42] Maria: last question: are there any security or compliance changes needed when we pin cache or change headers?
[10:50] Priya: no major changes. pinning uses request metadata and is encrypted in transit. for private deployments we'd need to confirm KMS keys and audit log retention, but for the hosted POC it's within SOC2 controls.
[11:05] Jordan: ok wrapping — recap and next steps.
[11:08] Priya: recap: (1) client caps + extended timeouts + jitter; (2) batch_size=12 for ingestion; (3) add X-Request-Id; (4) enable soft-quota to return 429s; (5) temporary +30% burst for scheduled load test; (6) Redwood to share incident timeline, runbook updates, and quantization eval.
[11:30] Ethan: will implement client caps and X-Request-Id today.
[11:34] Maria: i'll update the runbook with our side steps and share back.
[11:37] Jordan: great. we'll follow up with a post-mortem doc and assign action items. thanks everyone.
[11:45] End of recording.
